about.title: Redondo Beach Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Redondo Beach who leave a clinic or hospital feeling that something went wrong don't know whether they have a malpractice case or simply a bad result. That distinction matters under California law. A poor outcome by itself is not malpractice; the question is whether a provider fell below the accepted standard of care and that lapse caused harm. Answering it almost always takes a qualified medical expert reviewing your records. Los Angeles County has no shortage of hospitals, urgent care centers and specialty practices, and residents along Artesia Boulevard, Aviation Boulevard and the Route 1 corridor may be seen at several facilities before anyone notices an error. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles medical negligence claims and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Because MICRA sets tight timelines and a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement, an early conversation protects your options. Tell us what happened, and we'll make the connection.

whyChoose.title: What a Redondo Beach Malpractice Claim Involves

items.title: Two clocks run at once
items.desc: California's MICRA generally gives one year from when you discovered the injury, but never more than three years from when it happened. An attorney can pin down which date controls your situation before either passes.

items.title: Notice comes before any lawsuit
items.desc: State law requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to each provider you intend to sue. That step must be handled correctly and early, which is why waiting until the last month is a risk.

items.title: Expert review, not guesswork
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is almost always needed to establish that care fell below the standard. The attorneys in our network arrange that review and explain how the rising statutory cap on non-economic damages applies to your claim.

items.question: I was treated at an emergency room after a collision on Artesia Boulevard and a fracture was missed. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but a missed finding is not automatically negligence. The test is whether a reasonably careful provider in the same situation would have caught it, and whether the delay caused additional harm. Redondo Beach recorded 235 injury collisions in 2025, so emergency follow-up care is a common source of these questions. An attorney would have a medical expert review the imaging and records before advising you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Under MICRA, you generally have one year from the date you discovered, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury. There is also an outer limit of three years from the date of the injury itself, with narrow exceptions. Because a 90-day notice must go to the provider before filing, the practical deadline arrives sooner than the statute suggests. Contacting an attorney early keeps those dates manageable.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a Redondo Beach malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages such as pain and suffering in malpractice cases, and that cap increases each year under current law. Economic losses, including medical bills and lost income, are not subject to the same cap. An attorney can explain how the figure in effect at the time of your case would apply. No one can promise what any claim will be worth.
